quote.quote: The single biggest problem in communication is the illusion that it has taken place.
quote.author: George Bernard Shaw
quote.translation: 沟通中最大的问题在于人们错误地以为沟通已经发生了。
quote.explanation: 这句名言提醒我们，在职场中，仅仅发送信息或表达观点并不等同于有效沟通。真正的沟通需要确认对方是否准确理解，从而避免误解和冲突。

vocabulary.example: Effective collaboration requires clear communication and mutual trust among team members.
vocabulary.translation: 有效的协作需要团队成员之间清晰的沟通和相互信任。

vocabulary.example: If you cannot resolve the issue with your colleague, it may be necessary to escalate it to your manager.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你无法与同事解决问题，可能有必要将其上报给经理。

vocabulary.example: Before finalizing the project plan, we need to present it to all key stakeholders for feedback.
vocabulary.translation: 在最终确定项目计划之前，我们需要向所有关键利益相关者展示以获取反馈。

vocabulary.example: A concise email is more likely to be read and understood quickly by busy colleagues.
vocabulary.translation: 一封简洁的电子邮件更有可能被忙碌的同事快速阅读和理解。

vocabulary.example: Many workplace conflicts arise from simple miscommunication rather than actual disagreements.
vocabulary.translation: 许多职场冲突源于简单的沟通失误，而非真正的意见分歧。

vocabulary.example: Building rapport with clients helps establish trust and long-term business partnerships.
vocabulary.translation: 与客户建立融洽关系有助于建立信任和长期的商业伙伴关系。

vocabulary.example: We need to negotiate the terms of the contract before signing it.
vocabulary.translation: 在签署合同之前，我们需要协商条款。

vocabulary.definition: 善于表达的；清晰地表达
vocabulary.example: She is an articulate speaker who can present complex ideas in simple words.
vocabulary.translation: 她是一位善于表达的演讲者，能用简单的语言表达复杂的想法。

vocabulary.definition: 建设性的；有积极帮助的
vocabulary.example: I appreciate your constructive feedback on my presentation; it will help me improve.
vocabulary.translation: 我很感激你对我演示文稿的建设性反馈，这将帮助我改进。

vocabulary.example: After the meeting, please send a follow-up email summarizing the action items.
vocabulary.translation: 会议后，请发送一封跟进邮件总结待办事项。

pattern.pattern: I understand your point, but I’d like to suggest that...
pattern.example: I understand your point, but I’d like to suggest that we consider an alternative approach.
pattern.translation: 我理解你的观点，但我想建议我们考虑另一种方法。
pattern.usage: 用于在职场讨论中礼貌地表达不同意见或提出建议，先表示理解对方，再提出自己的观点，避免冲突。

grammar.title: 被动语态在职场沟通中的使用
grammar.explanation: 在职场英语中，被动语态常用于强调动作的接收者或结果，而非动作的执行者，从而显得更加客观或委婉。结构为：be + 过去分词 (+ by...)。例如：'The report was completed on time.' 而不是 'We completed the report on time.' 当不需要指出责任人时，被动语态尤为有用。
examples: A meeting will be scheduled for next Tuesday.
The decision has been made by the management.

pronunciation.tips: 重音在第二音节 'go'，注意 'ti' 发 /ʃi/ 而不是 /ti/，最后 'ate' 发 /eɪt/。

reading.title: The Art of Active Listening in the Workplace
reading.content: Active listening is one of the most underrated skills in professional communication. It goes beyond simply hearing words; it involves fully concentrating, understanding, responding, and remembering what the speaker says. In a team setting, active listening can prevent misunderstandings, build trust, and foster collaboration. For example, when a colleague shares a concern, instead of immediately offering advice, a good listener will paraphrase what was heard: 'So you're saying the deadline is too tight?' This confirms understanding and shows empathy. Studies show that teams with high active listening levels are more innovative and productive. To practice, maintain eye contact, avoid interrupting, and ask clarifying questions. Remember: communication is a two-way street; listening is just as important as speaking.
reading.translation: 主动倾听是职场沟通中最被低估的技能之一。它不仅仅是听到词语，而是充分集中注意力、理解、回应并记住说话者所说的内容。在团队环境中，主动倾听可以防止误解、建立信任并促进协作。例如，当同事分享担忧时，优秀的倾听者不会立即给出建议，而是转述所听到的内容：“你是说截止日期太紧了？”这能确认理解并表现出同理心。研究表明，拥有高度主动倾听能力的团队更具创新性和生产力。练习时，保持眼神交流、避免打断并提出澄清性问题。记住：沟通是双向的；倾听与说话同样重要。
